To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

teacher educators need to prepare prospective Tech Prep teachers to teach through application, student centered/inquiry based teaching, vocational/academic integration and collaboration, and real world experience.

teacher preparation needs to: 1. Develop teachers' ability to teach through application; 2. Develop teachers' skills in using inquiry based instruction; 3. Develop teachers' abilities to integrate academic and vocational education; 4. Develop teachers' collaboration and communication skills; and 5. Develop teachers' knowledge of and skills in real world experiences.

Tech Prep programs are being implemented in a variety of ways, that the majority of Tech Prep programs are implemented at the secondary level, that Tech Prep is being implemented in all subject areas, that there is no consensus on the definition of Tech Prep, that the most important aspect of Tech Prep is the application of academic and technical skills, that Tech Prep programs need to be more rigorous, that there is little or no collaboration between Tech Prep teachers, and that Tech Prep teachers need more training.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) What are the current reforms in general and vocational/technical education? (2) How can teacher preparation programs be modified to prepare teachers to implement Tech Prep?

the following questions: (1) What is the status of Tech Prep in the United States? (2) What are the major characteristics of Tech Prep programs and the people who work in them? (3) What are the perceptions of Tech Prep by the stakeholders? (4) What are the needs of Tech Prep teachers and teacher educators for teacher preparation? (5) What are the implications for teacher education?

the following: (1) What is happening in the area of science, math and English language arts? (2) What do teachers in Tech Prep programs think about their preparation? (3) What are the perceptions of Tech Prep stakeholders? and (4) What are the implications of Tech Prep for teacher education?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the research and synthesis efforts identified five major areas of need for prospective Tech Prep teachers: (1) application of knowledge, (2) student centered/inquiry based teaching, (3) integration of academic and vocational content, (4) collaborative work and (5) work experience.
Tech Prep teacher preparation is a "moving target," and that the needs and priorities are likely to change as the reform evolves.
teacher educators need to prepare teachers to teach in Tech Prep programs and that they need to prepare teachers for Tech Prep programs to be successful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
teacher preparation for Tech Prep needs to be reformed.
Tech Prep is a viable vehicle for reform and teacher education needs to be restructured in order to prepare teachers who will be successful in this environment.

Tech Prep is a viable reform vehicle for improving teacher preparation, but that the current state of the reform does not provide a sufficient basis for developing and supporting teacher education programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current teacher preparation system is ill suited for the demands of Tech Prep and, more generally, for the needs of the 21st century.
teacher preparation needs to focus on the skills and abilities that will enable prospective Tech Prep teachers to teach in a "Tech" Prep mode.
the principles and practices of Tech Prep have significant implications for the structure and content of teacher preparation programs.
